title.narrative: Food Security Emergency Response to mitigate the effects of floods in the Far North Region of Cameroon

description.narrative: In 2024, Cameroon experienced severe flooding, particularly in the Far North affecting 365,000 people in 67,000 households and destroying thousands of hectares of farmland. The worst-hit areas, Mayo-Danay and Logone-et-Chari, account for 98% of the flood-affected population. This disaster compounds the country’s already fragile situation, with 3.4 million people needing humanitarian assistance due to ongoing crises. The loss of 5,278 livestock and the destruction of 82,509 hectares of farmland have further exacerbated food insecurity, especially during the lean season.According to meteorological forecasts, the Far North and parts of the North region have received 25% more rainfall than the seasonal average, with more expected in October. The flooding threatens to worsen if rivers such as Logone and Chari overflow, potentially breaching dikes and displacing even more people.In response, WFP will provide emergency food assistance to 6,303 flood-affected individuals in Mayo-Danay, offering three months of support through cash-based transfers (CBT) at 9,000 XAF per person per day for 3 months. This intervention aims to stabilize food security, protect livelihoods, and address the immediate nutritional needs of vulnerable populations, including children. By mitigating the current food crisis, the project also seeks to prevent a larger humanitarian disaster and set the foundation for recovery interventions and long-term resilience building.
